blocks.body: Fixtures below the sewer line, like a basement bathroom or laundry, drain into a sealed basin. The ejector pump lifts that wastewater into the main line. A float starts it and a check valve stops water from falling back. If one part fails, those fixtures back up.

blocks.h2: Is It the Pump or the System?
blocks.body: When basement fixtures back up, the pump gets the blame, but it's not always the pump. A stuck float keeps a good pump from starting. A failed check valve lets water fall back so the pump runs nonstop. A clogged vent makes the basin gurgle and smell. Wipes wrapped around the impeller can stall it. We open the basin, test each part and replace only what failed. If the pump is old and worn, we'll tell you that too.

blocks.h2: Ejector Pump Questions From Hanover Park Homeowners

items.q: My ejector pump alarm is going off. What now?
items.preview: Stop using basement fixtures and call us.
items.answer: Stop using every fixture that drains to the basin and call us.

items.q: How long do ejector pumps last?
Can I flush wipes into an ejector system?
items.answer: No. Wipes, even flushable ones, are the top cause of pump failure.

items.q: Why does it smell like sewer near the pit?
items.preview: A seal, vent or dry trap.
items.answer: Usually a worn lid seal, a vent issue or a dry floor drain trap.

items.q: Can I use the basement bathroom during a power outage?
items.answer: Not much. The pump can't run, so the basin fills. Go easy until power returns.

items.q: Can an ejector pump have a battery backup?
items.answer: Some can. Ask us about options for your basin.

items.q: How much does ejector pump replacement cost in Hanover Park?
items.preview: It depends on the pump and basin. You'll approve a flat price first.
items.answer: It depends on the pump, the basin and access. You'll approve a flat-rate price before we start.
